record.paper_title: Some open problems on Banach spaces
record.original_question: Let E be a Kothe Banach space on [0,1], meaning a Banach space E contained in L^1[0,1] with 1_[0,1] in E and the lattice ideal property that |x| <= |y| with y in E implies x in E and ||x|| <= ||y||. Assume E has absolutely continuous norm on the unit, let X be a Banach space, and let T:E -> X be bounded linear. Is there an appropriately chosen infinite-dimensional subspace Z of E such that, whenever T is Z-strictly singular, T must be narrow? Here Z-strictly singular means that the restriction of T to any subspace of E isomorphic to Z is not an into-isomorphism.

evidence.quote: By a K¨othe Banach space on [0, 1] we mean a Banach space E ⊆ L1, 1[0,1] ∈ E and for each x ∈ L1 and y ∈ E the condition |x| ≤ |y| implies x ∈ E and kxk ≤ kyk.
Z-strictly singular if Z is an infinite dimensional Banach space, and the restriction T|Y of T to any subspace Y of E isomorphic to Z is not an into-isomorphism.
Problem 8.3. Does T have to be narrow, provided that T is Z-strictly singular for an appropriately chosen infinite dimensional subspace Z of E?
E is assumed to be a K¨othe Banach space on [0, 1] with an absolutely continuous norm on the unit, X a Banach space and T ∈ L(E, X).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Definitions. A Köthe Banach space on [0,1] is a Banach space E with E ⊆ L¹[0,1] such that the constant function 1_{[0,1]} belongs to E and such that whenever x ∈ L¹[0,1], y ∈ E, and |x| ≤ |y| almost everywhere, one has x ∈ E and ‖x‖_E ≤ ‖y‖_E. The space E is said to have an absolutely continuous norm on the unit if ‖1_A‖_E → 0 whenever A ⊆ [0,1] are measurable sets with Lebesgue measure tending to 0.

A bounded linear operator T : E → X into a Banach space X is called narrow if for every measurable set A ⊆ [0,1] and every ε > 0 there exists a function x ∈ E with x = x·1_A, ∫₀¹ x dt = 0, |x| = 1_A almost everywhere, and ‖T x‖_X < ε.

Given an infinite-dimensional Banach space Z, the operator T is called Z-strictly singular if, for every closed subspace Y of E that is isomorphic (as a Banach space) to Z, the restriction T|_Y is not an isomorphism into X.

Question. Let E be a Köthe Banach space on [0,1] with an absolutely continuous norm on the unit, let X be a Banach space, and let T : E → X be a bounded linear operator. Does there exist a choice of an infinite-dimensional Banach space Z (allowed to depend on E, X, T) such that Z-strict singularity of T implies that T is narrow?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches identified active work on narrow vs. Z-strictly singular operators (e.g., results showing ℓ²-strictly singular operators from L_p are narrow, partially addressing a question of Plichko), but no source was found that resolves the general problem of finding, for an arbitrary Köthe Banach space E with absolutely continuous norm on the unit and an arbitrary bounded operator T : E → X, a subspace Z whose strict singularity forces narrowness. The status appears unresolved in this generality.

status_evidence.title: Narrow and ℓ2-strictly singular operators from Lp
status_evidence.snippet: Every ℓ2-strictly singular operator from Lp (1<p<∞) to any Banach space with an unconditional basis is narrow, partially answering a question of Plichko.
status_evidence.claim: A partial result is known for E = L_p with Z = ℓ², but the general Köthe-space question remains beyond this special case.

status_evidence.title: On two definitions of a narrow operator on Köthe–Bochner spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies coincidence of definitions of narrow operators on Köthe–Bochner spaces with order continuous norm.
status_evidence.claim: Research on narrow operators in Köthe spaces is ongoing without addressing this specific problem.
